chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever teaches a good thing, for him is a reward like that of the one who acts upon it.'
I said: 'What if he (in turn) teaches it to others — does that (reward) flow for him?' He said: 'If he were to teach it to all of the people, it would still flow for him.'
I said: 'What if he has died?' He said: 'And even if he has died.'

key_terms.أَجْر: reward, recompense — the spiritual merit accrued for good deeds
key_terms.خَيْراً: a good thing — encompasses beneficial knowledge, righteous practice, and moral guidance
key_terms.عَلَّمَ: taught, instructed — the active transmission of knowledge
key_terms.يَجْرِي / جَرَى: to flow, to run — metaphor for continuous, ongoing reward

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the reward for teaching good things?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that the reward for spreading beneficial knowledge is perpetual — the teacher receives the same reward as every person who acts upon what they learned, and this reward continues flowing even after the teacher's death. This teaching was transmitted through Abu Baseer, a close companion of the Imam, who heard it directly. It reflects the Islamic principle that beneficial knowledge is a form of ongoing charity (sadaqa jariya) whose reward outlasts the lifetime of the one who spreads it.
